cases.feature: F040-03 Fine-tune replies (warmth, enthusiasm, formality, length, headings, emoji, technical depth)
cases.evidence:
The Chrome extension (apps/extension) has no code for the dials. A grep of apps/extension/src and apps/extension/manifest.json for warmth, enthusiasm, response style, personalization, custom instructions, response length and technical level found nothing. The extension has no settings UI for any of them, and it never builds a response-style block. I did not search apps/extension/__tests__.

The effect still reaches Chrome replies through the server. Chrome managed chat posts to the hosted gateway at apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts:112 (/api/llm/v1/chat/completions); apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/cloudAgentClient.ts:317 posts to the same path. I did not check which endpoint the managed chat handler itself calls.

On that endpoint, apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:3993-3997 calls buildCustomInstructionsPreamble unless the surface is 'api' or personalization is false. I did not trace the surface that Chrome's requests resolve to (resolveAuthenticatedSurface, line 3694); line 3184 shows the server does treat a 'chrome' surface. The function is in apps/web/lib/server/user-identity.ts:250-286. It turns the account's saved personalization (formatResponseStyleLines, line 146) into the <response_style> block (lines 192-193). That block covers warmth, enthusiasm, headers and lists, emoji, length and technical level from the contracts file. There is no separate formality dial; the feature page says formal tone is a preset. I did not run anything, so I cannot confirm Chrome replies actually change.

For the seven requirement items (S40.06, S40.07, S40.09 to S40.13), the 'replies follow it' half is probably met through the account, and the 'user can set it' half is missing on this app. Preferences are set on web, desktop or mobile.

The ledger's 'partial' fits this. The feature page's 'missing' (implementation chrome: missing) misses the server-side application of the account's preferences to Chrome chat.

cases.feature: F060-01 Start a task from a goal (S60.01, S60.03, S60.04)
cases.evidence:
The AGI Work path is absent from VS Code, but a different goal-to-agent-run entry exists, so the feature page's "missing" is too strong.

Absent (the feature page's claim):
- `rg "agiwork|agi_work|work_mode|agi_work_goal"` over apps/extension-vscode/src and package.json returned nothing.
- No constraints or deliverable input exists in the start flow. The only `deliverables` hit in src is a read-only listing of run artifacts (src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudRunDetail.ts:141).
- S60.04 (the user specifies a deliverable and the run receives it) is therefore not met on VS Code. The ledger also says missing for it.

Present (what the feature page overlooked):
- Command `agi-workforce.continueInCloud`, titled "Code: Continue in the Cloud", is in apps/extension-vscode/package.json:592-593. It is also reachable from the surface menu (src/features/surfaces/surfaceMenu.ts:136) and from a sidebar webview message (src/features/sidebar-webview/ChatStateManager.ts:1817).
- The handler is src/features/cloud-tasks/continueInCloud.ts:93. It does the following:
  - It prompts "What should the cloud session do on <branch>?" and reads the goal from an input box (lines 108-115).
  - It shows a modal review of the model and source (lines 125-131).
  - It calls `api.create` for a Cloud Code session titled from the goal (lines 142-153).
  - It calls `api.startAgentTurn(sessionId, { goal, model, ... })` (line 169), which starts a real cloud agent turn from the stated goal.
- The package.json description at line 847 says this hands the branch to a cloud session.
- Cloud tasks started on any device are listed, opened, approved, rejected and pulled into the workspace (package.json:533-563, 1122-1158).
- S60.01 (a dedicated entry that starts a real agent run) and S60.03 (the objective is stated and used as the session goal and title) are therefore partly met.

Limits:
- This is a Cloud Code session, not an AGI Work run. It sends no work_mode and no structured goal object with constraints, deliverable or excluded tools. It needs a git workspace with a branch.
- docs/product/experience-contract.md:635 marks AGI Work run N/A on VS Code, so the feature page's narrow AGI Work reading is defensible. The ledger's "partial" matches the code better.
- I read the code only and ran nothing, so nobody has confirmed the flow works.

cases.feature: F067-08 Work from an issue or a team mention (S67.34)
cases.evidence:
There is no desktop-native @mention intake. The real GitHub mention-to-task path is server-side in the web app: apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:213 calls githubMentionTask, and apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-github-task.ts implements runGitHubCodeTask. The Electron desktop loads the hosted web app (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:345 win.loadURL), so the Cloud session page that the GitHub reply links to opens inside desktop. That is a real but shared path, not code owned by the desktop.

The desktop does have its own surfaces that start agent work from an issue or a team chat, which is why "partial" fits better than "missing".
- apps/desktop/src/features/schedules/DesktopScheduleTriggersPanel.tsx:4,42-47 offers a GitHub trigger source using MANAGED_CLOUD_GITHUB_TRIGGER_EVENT_TYPES. That list includes 'issues.opened' (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/triggers.ts:17-28). A person can set up a managed Cloud run that fires when an issue opens on an installed repository.
- apps/desktop/src/features/settings/cloud/CloudSlackSection.tsx:30 and DesktopCloudSettingsModal.tsx:1254 manage the Slack app, described as "mention it in a channel, and it answers there". The settings page only opens /settings/slack in the browser. The Slack intake itself is in apps/web/lib/slack/slack-events.ts. I did not confirm that a Slack mention starts a coding task.

Gaps that keep it from being full. The desktop has no @mention parsing and no coding-task intake of its own. The issues.opened trigger is not a mention. A Slack mention is not confirmed to start a coding session.

The feature page's "missing" is too strong, because it searched only for the GitHub mention path and did not look at the desktop's trigger and Slack surfaces. The ledger's "partial" is supported. Nothing was run, so none of this has been seen working.
